title: OCF
description: Schema for the three Open Course Format (OCF) document types, version 0.2.0: course.json, module.json, and lesson.json.

content_hash.description: Optional sha256 hash of the referenced document, formatted "sha256-{hex}". Lets a consumer detect when an externally-referenced document has changed since this reference was last pinned (integrity, caching, reproducible progress tracking), the same way Subresource Integrity works on the web. Omit for co-located `path` references, already versioned by this repo's own history.

ocf_version.description: Any 0.2.x patch release of OCF — see the Versioning & Conformance policy for what's allowed to change in a patch.

status.description: Content lifecycle stage. Absent is equivalent to "published" — this field exists for a consumer that wants to hide draft/deprecated content or a course author's own tooling, not to gate access by itself.

estimated_mins.description: Same unit as module.estimated_mins and lesson.estimated_mins, for trivial roll-up across all three levels.

outcomes.description: What a learner will be able to do after completing this course — distinct from description, which is a general summary. Each entry is one outcome statement, e.g. "Write and deploy a basic REST API in Python." Purely descriptive metadata for display; not machine-checked against any content.

modules.description: Ordered list; array order determines the course's module sequence.

ocf_version.description: Any 0.2.x patch release of OCF — see the Versioning & Conformance policy for what's allowed to change in a patch.

estimated_mins.description: Same unit as lesson.estimated_mins, so a consumer can sum lessons or use the module's own figure interchangeably.

outcomes.description: What a learner will be able to do after completing this module — same convention as course.outcomes, at module granularity.

lessons.description: Ordered list; array order determines the module's lesson sequence.

ocf_version.description: Any 0.2.x patch release of OCF — see the Versioning & Conformance policy for what's allowed to change in a patch.

articles.description: Written content for this lesson (OAF documents). A lesson's content is this collection, plus video_lessons and practice_sets — there is no separate content.md on the lesson itself.

path.description: Path, relative to lesson.json, to a co-located article.

article_url.description: Full URL to an article.json hosted in a separate repo.

video_lessons.description: Video content for this lesson (OVF documents).

path.description: Path, relative to lesson.json, to a co-located video lesson.

video_lesson_url.description: Full URL to a video.json hosted in a separate repo.

practice_sets.description: Practice content for this lesson (OPF sets).

path.description: Path, relative to lesson.json, to a co-located OPF set's set.json.

set_url.description: Full URL to a set.json hosted in a separate repo.

related.description: Suggested material for a learner who wants to go further after this lesson — a related video, a recommended book, a downloadable file, another course. Written and video content that's actually part of this lesson belongs in articles[]/video_lessons[] instead; this is for material the lesson merely points at.

related_item.description: A suggested piece of material for the learner to explore further. Either an OES-native pointer (`path` or one of the `*_url` fields, the same idiom used by every other cross-reference in OES, so a consuming app can fetch it and render it richly — real duration, thumbnail, etc.) or a fully external pointer (a bare `url`) for anything not itself modeled as OES content, e.g. a YouTube video or a book's product page.

type.description: What kind of thing this is, independent of how it's addressed below.

path.description: Path to co-located OES content (a video.json, article.json, set.json, or course.json) this entry points at.

url.description: For material not modeled as OES content at all — e.g. a YouTube video, an external article, a book's product page.

note.description: Why this is suggested, e.g. "if you want a deeper dive into the underlying math".

source.description: Where this content was originally sourced or adapted from, if it wasn't authored directly for OES — e.g. produced by an importer against another platform's course structure. Entirely optional; omit for content authored directly. Distinct from this document's own top-level `license`, where present — that describes this OES document's license, not what it was adapted from, and the original may be more restrictive (or simply different) — see `source.license` instead.

url.description: The original content's own URL — a course's syllabus page, a lecture's page, etc.

platform.description: Free-text label for the originating platform or site, e.g. "Khan Academy", "MIT OpenCourseWare". Deliberately not an enum — OES doesn't hard-code or endorse any specific platform; any importer fills in whatever's accurate.

license.description: The ORIGINAL content's license or terms of use at the source. Free text, not constrained to SPDX like this document's own `license` field — many platforms' terms of use aren't expressible as a single SPDX identifier.

retrieved_at.description: When this content was fetched/adapted from the source — provenance, and a signal for how stale this copy might be.

note.description: Free-text context an importer or author wants to record — adaptation details, attribution requirements, anything not covered by the fields above.
